item.description:
Directed by: Katherine Wilkinson | Written by William Shakespeare Troilus and Cressida (play) is a dark, satirical take on love and war during the Trojan War. Troilus and Cressida’s romance is tested when she is traded to the Greek camp, while warriors and leaders on both sides reveal ambition, ego, and moral decay. The play questions heroism, loyalty, and what’s left of love in a world defined by conflict.

item.description:
For nearly six decades, this New Jersey couple had a front-row seat to the world of fine things. She ran estate sales across the state for more than 40 years, and in his retirement years he ran an art gallery. Their trained eyes and lifelong love of beautiful, well-made objects are reflected throughout their home: museum-quality paintings, Oriental and Native American rugs, period furniture, fine jewelry and crystal, alongside the playful finds of true collectors, including antique trains, vintage toys, a pool table, and a workshop full of old tools. item.title: Everything Book Club, "Life & Death & Giants" by Ron Rindo — Tue Dec 8, 1:15 PM — Montclair Main - Teen Room
item.description:
An American tall tale with a surprising plot and the heart of a giant. Gabriel Fisher is born an orphan, weighing 18 pounds and measuring 27 inches long. Gabriel gets taken in by his devout Amish grandparents who try to protect him from the "English" world. But it’s hard to hide when you’re nearly 8 feet tall. When Gabriel reaches 17, the local football coach spots him tossing hay bales like sofa cushions. What happens next transforms not only Gabriel’s life but the lives of everyone he meets.
"'Life, and Death, and Giants' is an intriguing and alluring novel from beginning to end....Reading it is like meeting a family that you never knew existed and becoming close friends in a few weeks. Highly recommended." --Jane Smiley
RON RINDO is a professor of English and creative writing at the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh. He has published one previous novel, "Breathing Lake Superior, "and three short story collections. He lives in Pickett, Wisconsin.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.

item.title: Manual Cinema: The 4th Witch — Thu Feb 18, 7:30 PM
item.description:
Run Time: 65 minutes
Manual Cinema’s The 4th Witch is a fantastic new tale, inspired by elements of Shakespeare’s Macbeth, in which a girl escapes war and flees into a dark forest. Told through shadow puppetry, actors in silhouette and live music (without dialogue or narration), The 4th Witch begins on the eve of an invasion of a small town by the local warlord, Macbeth. The girl flees the invading army and escapes into the nearby forest. Orphaned and exiled, she is rescued by a witch, who adopts her as an apprentice. As she becomes more skilled in witchcraft, her grief and rage draw her into a nightmarish quest for vengeance against the warlord who killed her parents: Macbeth.
The 4th Witch, an inversion of Shakespeare’s Macbeth, explores themes of grief, war, generational conflict, and cycles of violence through the collateral damage left behind on the battleground. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Dec 2, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Book Talk: 20 Over 60 by Beth Weinhouse and David Galef — Thu Dec 3, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Conference Room
item.description:
In their new anthology 20 OVER 60 (Regal House; October 6, 2026), editors Beth Weinhouse and David Galef—also co-editors of the anthology 20 OVER 40—present a portrait of later life that is consistently overlooked, in a culture obsessed with youth. The twenty short stories—including ones by Joyce Carol Oates, Paul Theroux, and Jane Gardam—are vibrant, moving, and often hilarious, capturing the texture of life after sixty in all its complexity.
Among the characters readers will meet: a retired couple whose hobby is stealing pepper mills from high-end restaurants, a woman juggling her husband and ex-husband staying in the same hospital, a futuristic nursing home whose designers become its unhappy residents, an older woman trying her hand at online dating, and a grandfather helping his granddaughter scatter her mother's ashes.
